purpose: Archive against link rot the one verified public instance of operated SCATS data for Newcastle (design/signalling/08-operated-signal-data-discovery.md; issue #78 route 2, adopted by user direction 25 Aug 2026). Operated cycle-time evidence for the A.signals sweep basis: corridor-adjacent TCS 1138 (Hunter/Steel) 72-81 s, parallel arterial TCS 923 (King/Steel) 104-113 s, vs the assumed 110 s swept 80-140 s.

PPSHCC-137_643_hunter_st_tia.pdf.document: Traffic Impact Assessment, 643 Hunter Street, Newcastle West; The Transport Planning Partnership for Next Level Seven Pty Ltd; TTPP ref 22106, V03, 1 September 2022; exhibited as PPSHCC-137
PPSHCC-137_643_hunter_st_tia.pdf.note: Appendix E: TCS plans for TCS 923 (King/Steel) and TCS 1138 (Hunter/Steel). Appendix F: SCATS Interpreted History, 24 h of 15-minute periodic statistics for both sites, Tuesday 19 July 2022. Appendix G: pedestrian call proportions. NEITHER site is one of the 14 modelled corridor intersections (A2 scats_site_id list) - evidence for the sweep basis, never a registry value. The signalling dossier's file 08 recorded the site address as '121 Hunter St'; the document itself says 643 Hunter Street, Newcastle West (corrected in the dossier in the same change that landed this record).

verification: PDF header %PDF-1.7; 245 pages extracted; TTPP reference 22106 on the quality record page; Appendix E/F markers and TCS site ids 923 and 1138 located in the text layer.
channel_note: Channel is per-intersection and opportunistic: TIAs republish TfNSW-supplied SCATS material for the intersections each development assessed.
